summary: Single-stage planning pass for local resolution invariants. The accepted aggregate R09.7 packet already owns all twenty-one core targets assigned to R09.7b, and the accepted R09.7a supplement owns the regular-to-completed coefficient comparison. This packet supplies their stage-level ownership and dependency manifest, a corrected standalone reader and a compact native-carrier suggested file. It creates no duplicate declaration nodes. The stage is planned, with inherited supplier interfaces and implementation refinements stated explicitly; nothing is claimed implemented.

dependencyClosure.rule: Every direct prerequisite of an imported target is either another imported target, one of the nine imported support nodes, a pinned declaration, or the SF.0 interface. The support nodes additionally import the existing StableReduction Layer 4 blowup interface and SF.3 Cartier bridge. Accepted owners retain responsibility for their prerequisite chains; the manifest does not re-review them.
dependencyClosure.consumer: AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.7c consumes semicoherent invariant strata and local augmented descent to construct and glue global centres and prove global termination.

inheritedInterfaces.need: One actual regular étale coordinate neighbourhood at each closed point, residue-field coordinate completions, compatible extension of coordinate derivations and restriction to contact, quotient and finite-ideal completion comparison, and faithful-flat reflection of finite ideal equality and power inclusion. Retain the imported Jacobson finite-type closed-point density bridge; independently chosen formal germs do not supply common regular presentations.

Existing ordinary blowup universal property, complement isomorphism, strict-transform saturation, exceptional Cartier ideal and pivot chart comparisons. Coordinate permissible centres supply controlled divisibility and cancellation; a blowup is not assumed flat.

Native effective-Cartier local equations and the ideal-product/divisor dictionary used by labelled SNC boundaries. Current Tau Ceti already has Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsEffectiveCartier beyond the pin; reuse it. No new Cartier or blowup theory is proposed here.

remaining: Discharge the inherited SF.0 regular-coordinate, actual-completion, derivation/restriction and faithful-flat comparison interface; use residue fields at non-rational closed points.
Connect the imported presentation/transform carriers to StableReduction Layer 4 ordinary blowups and the native Cartier/SNC bridge; do not duplicate either supplier.

Implement and prove the accepted local targets and their APIs/tests, including common-neighbourhood semicoherence, pointed exceptional tests, birth history and codimension normalization. All implementations remain unchecked.
At assembly/package time retain the accepted owner ids and synchronize their older readers with accepted review corrections. Compact native examples here do not replace the full geometric targets.

importedSourceIssues.locator: BM1997 Example 2.1, p. 226, year-one parenthetical pullback
importedSourceIssues.appliedCorrection: The pulled-back year-zero monomial is x₁²x₂³. Its x₁ pivot transform after division by the square is y₁³y₂³. This is an existing independently confirmed finding, not a new report.

importedSourceIssues.locator: BM1997 proof of Theorem 9.6, p. 282; compare Definition 7.9, p. 265, and Remark 9.5(1), p. 277
importedSourceIssues.appliedCorrection: Use |β|<dᵢ−|γ| in the coefficient derivative ideal. The non-strict bound adds a unit for c=t², mark two. This is an existing independently confirmed finding, not a new report.

prototypeOmissions: The fixed WORKERS.md shape governs this file. No second heavy marked-presentation, test-equivalence, Samuel-certificate, history, word or geometric invariant carrier is introduced merely to make signatures possible at the pins.

The reader specifies every imported definition, its planning API and discriminating tests. The suggested file states only native power-series/ideal examples and a finite rational monomial pivot inequality. It does not restate the full inherited API as stand-ins.

Formal derivative coefficient extraction is a native specialization of the imported completion comparison. It does not prove existence of the geometric completion maps, their compatibilities or faithful-flat reflection.

Global centres, termination, resolution outputs and arbitrary smooth-morphism functoriality are not asserted by these local examples. R09.7c owns the first three; BM1997 local-isomorphism invariance does not supply the last.
